qs.q: A 62-year-old man undergoes a standard Whipple procedure for a resectable adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head. On postoperative day five, he develops a high-output, amylase-rich fluid collection from his abdominal drain. What is the most common serious complication that has occurred?
qs.e: Pancreatic fistula from the pancreatic anastomosis is the commonest serious complication following a Whipple procedure. Delayed gastric emptying and bile leaks also occur, but they are less frequent than pancreatic leaks.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 56-year-old woman undergoes a Whipple procedure for a resectable periampullary tumour. When designing the single jejunal limb reconstruction, which three anastomoses must be sequentially fashioned onto this limb?
qs.e: Reconstruction after a Whipple procedure involves a pancreaticojejunostomy, hepaticojejunostomy, and gastrojejunostomy on a single jejunal limb. Pancreaticogastrostomy is an alternative to pancreaticojejunostomy, but not part of the standard triple anastomosis sequence.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 70-year-old woman is evaluated in a high-volume surgical centre for a suspected periampullary tumour requiring a Whipple procedure. Provided the operation is performed by experienced multidisciplinary teams, what is her expected perioperative mortality rate?
qs.e: Perioperative mortality for a Whipple procedure is under 5% in high-volume centres. This low mortality rate reflects specialized surgical expertise and postoperative critical care management.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 62-year-old man with a locally advanced, borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma is prescribed gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel before his planned Whipple procedure. What is the primary clinical rationale for administering this drug regimen prior to surgery?
o: To eliminate any microscopic systemic spread
To provide immediate relief of biliary pain
To shrink the tumor and improve operability
To eradicate the primary local tumor mass
qs.e: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is administered before surgery specifically to reduce tumor volume and facilitate a complete resection. Adjuvant therapy, rather than neoadjuvant, is primarily intended to target microscopic residual disease.
qs.s: Oncology: Surgery, Radiotherapy & Chemotherapy Explained: MCQs

qs.q: During a Whipple procedure for a pancreatic head tumor, the surgeon identifies the major duodenal papilla. Into which specific anatomical segment does this structure open?
qs.e: The major duodenal papilla is located in the descending or second part of the duodenum, where the hepatopancreatic ampulla empties. The first part of the duodenum is devoid of these major duct openings.
